questions.prompt: What is the test object of system testing?
options: A single function
The interfaces between two components only
The whole integrated system
The business process in the customer's organisation only
questions.explanation: System testing looks at the complete, integrated system's behaviour and capabilities. Functions are component level, interfaces are integration level.

questions.prompt: System testing covers both functional and non-functional characteristics, such as performance and usability.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: ISTQB describes system testing as covering end-to-end tasks and non-functional characteristics of the whole system.

options: A separate ISTQB test level after acceptance testing
A test that follows a complete user or business journey through every layer and system it touches
Testing one API endpoint
Testing the database schema
questions.explanation: End-to-end is a scope or style of test, not one of the ISTQB test levels. It follows full journeys across UI, services, data and external systems.

questions.prompt: For an end-to-end 'place order' test, where should outcomes be verified? Select all that apply.
options: The order confirmation screen
The order record in the database or admin view
The payment provider sandbox transaction
The confirmation email in a test mail catcher
questions.explanation: An end-to-end test verifies every system the journey touches. A correct screen with a missing payment record or email is still a failure.

questions.prompt: Your staging environment differs from production in several ways. Which difference is the highest risk for an order flow?
options: Staging has a different background colour on the login page
Staging uses a fake payment stub that always approves, while production uses the real provider with 3-D Secure
Staging has fewer product images
Staging's servers are in a different time zone and nothing is time-based
questions.explanation: Payment integration behaves very differently under real provider rules, so a stub that always approves hides whole classes of failures. The other differences have little impact on this flow.

questions.prompt: Why should end-to-end tests be few?
options: They cannot find defects
They are slow, depend on many systems and break more easily, so they should focus on critical journeys while detail is tested at lower levels
ISTQB forbids more than 10
They are always manual
questions.explanation: E2E tests are expensive and brittle. The test pyramid recommends many fast low-level tests and a small set of E2E tests on business-critical journeys.

questions.prompt: An automated E2E test logs in, adds an item, pays and asserts only that the URL contains '/thank-you'. A defect created orders with total 0.00 and it still passed. What was missing?
options: A longer wait
Assertions on business outcomes: the order total, payment amount and stored order
Running it in a different browser
A screenshot on success
questions.explanation: Asserting only navigation lets wrong data pass. Checkpoints should verify the totals and records the journey is meant to produce.

questions.prompt: A team has 400 system tests, all automated through the UI, and runs take 6 hours. Which split best improves speed without losing coverage?
options: Keep all 400 at UI level
Move field validation and business-rule checks to API/component level, keep about a dozen UI journeys end to end, and keep non-functional system tests on a production-like environment
Delete half the tests at random
Move all tests to unit level
questions.explanation: Coverage stays but moves to the cheapest layer that can detect each defect. E2E keeps critical journeys. Random deletion loses coverage; unit tests alone cannot test an integrated system.

questions.prompt: Orders pass every staging test but in production customers never get confirmation emails. Staging uses a fake email service. What is the best long-term improvement?
options: Stop sending emails in production

Use a production-like email path in staging (the real provider's sandbox or the real integration routed to a safe test inbox), document remaining environment differences as risks, and add a production monitoring check for email delivery
Ask customers to report missing emails
Test emails manually in production with real customer addresses
questions.explanation: The environment gap caused the escape. Closing it safely, recording other gaps as risks and monitoring after release addresses the root cause. Testing with real customer addresses is unsafe.
